summary: This large survey maps agent memory through a forms-functions-dynamics taxonomy, distinguishing factual, experiential, and working memory as well as token-level, parametric, and latent representations.
why_it_matters: It is one of the broadest memory surveys in the vault and useful as a reference map for comparing memory systems across representation, purpose, and lifecycle.
method_setup: The paper formalizes agent memory relative to LLM memory and RAG, surveys memory forms and lifecycle operations, and compiles benchmarks and open-source frameworks for memory-augmented agents.
key_claims: Memory should be treated as a first-class primitive of agent design.
Different memory forms align with different functional roles and dynamics.
Future agent memory research needs stronger support for multimodal, shared, and trustworthy memory.
limitations: The scope is extremely broad, so many systems are described at a high level.
The survey is stronger as a field map than as an empirical comparison of competing memory designs.
builds_on_unresolved: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
A Human-Inspired Reading Agent with Gist Memory of Very Long Contexts
